root_cause.text: The `hid_bpf_hw_request` function in the HID-BPF subsystem trusts the return value of the BPF hook dispatch without validating that it does not exceed the destination buffer's size, leading to a potential out-of-bounds write during `memcpy`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (ret > size) ret = size;` before `memcpy(buf, dma_data, ret)` in `drivers/hid/bpf/hid_bpf_dispatch.c`, and the commit message notes that the return value of `dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests()` can be arbitrarily large and lacks guarantees of validity.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 91a7f802d1852f60139712bdcfa98db547ce0531
Author: Benjamin Tissoires <bentiss@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Nov 3 16:57:49 2022 +0100

    HID: bpf: introduce hid_hw_request()
    
    This function can not be called under IRQ, thus it is only available
    while in SEC("syscall").
    For consistency, this function requires a HID-BPF context to work with,
    and so we also provide a helper to create one based on the HID unique
    ID.
    
    Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfound
bic_trace_step.reason: The function `hid_bpf_hw_request` is introduced in this commit. In lines 333-334, it performs `memcpy(buf, dma_data, ret)` if `ret > 0`. However, there is no validation to ensure that `ret` does not exceed `buf__sz` (the size of the destination buffer `buf` and the allocated source buffer `dma_data`). If `ret` is larger than `buf__sz`, this leads to an out-of-bounds read from `dma_data` and an out-of-bounds write to `buf`.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `hid_bpf_hw_request`, `dma_data` is allocated with size `buf__sz` (via `kmemdup(buf, buf__sz, GFP_KERNEL)`). After calling `hid_bpf_ops->hid_hw_raw_request`, the return value `ret` is used directly in `memcpy(buf, dma_data, ret)` if `ret > 0` (lines 331-332). There is no check to ensure that `ret` does not exceed `buf__sz`, which can lead to an out-of-bounds write to `buf` and an out-of-bounds read from `dma_data`.
